correctness.rationale: For every finite simple real unicyclic G including disconnected forests, Fourier projection is minimax after averaging all sign translations; coordinate Hahn–Banach extends the upper bound to all isometric superspaces, proving absolute equality lambda=E|sum edge-characters|. The edge homomorphism has exactly the unique circuit relation and uniform fibres, giving conditional density 1+prod_cycle. Global sign reversal annihilates odd-k correction. For even k=2s, two-sign averaging localizes the absolute value discrete second difference to central/near-central slices; exact elementary-symmetric even coefficients give (-1)^(s-1)binom(floor((m-2)/2),s-1)/binom(m-2,2s-2). Multiplying central binomial probability yields displayed exact correction, nonvanishing sign and Stirling fixed-even-k decay. No reliance on finite enumeration for all-size claim.
residual_risks: The displayed asymptotic is for fixed even k as m tends to infinity; no uniform joint-k limit is claimed.
No statement for complex scalars, weighted kernels, multicyclic graphs, or arbitrary Lp extremizers.

value.rationale: The real edge-Walsh projection constant is a natural Banach invariant for a graph-parametrized family. Classifying every one-cycle graph using only edge count m and circuit length k, with all forest attachments invisible, a mod-four alternating exact correction, explicit 6-edge values and a sharp fixed-cycle decay, provides a usable structural benchmark beyond a generic Walsh expectation formula. The central-slice calculation is motivated by the unique cycle relation, not an arbitrary finite slice or preexisting table entry.
residual_risks: This is a specialized exact invariant, not a theorem for weighted/multicyclic graphs; broader significance should not be exaggerated.
Possible historical closed parity first-moment formulas could reduce its originality and hence value upon further source discovery.

final_claim: For every finite simple undirected graph with cycle-space dimension one, m edges and unique cycle length k (3<=k<=m), the real edge-Walsh absolute projection constant is A_m for odd k; for even k=2s it equals A_m+(-1)^(s-1) B_m * binom(floor((m-2)/2),s-1)/binom(m-2,2s-2), where A_m=m binom(m-1,floor((m-1)/2))/2^(m-1) and B_m=binom(m-2,floor((m-2)/2))/2^(m-2). Its even correction is nonzero and asymptotic at fixed s>=2 to (-1)^(s-1)(2s-3)!! sqrt(2/pi) m^(-s+1/2). Tree attachments/disconnected forests change nothing if m,k are fixed.
limitations: No all-size computer enumeration: proof is analytical.
